**Allowed origins**

CORS is set up in `worker/src/index.ts:19-35`. The `origin` callback inside `cors({...})` returns the request's origin only if one of these is true:
- It is exactly `http://localhost:4200`, the local Angular dev server.
- It ends with `.pages.dev`.
- It ends with `.workers.dev`. This covers the deployed frontend at `https://ai-dnd-frontend.ai-dnd.workers.dev`.

Any other origin gets `null`, so no CORS headers are sent and the browser blocks the call. A request with no `Origin` header also gets `null`. That means non-browser clients like curl aren't affected by CORS.

Other CORS settings in the same block:
- Methods: `GET`, `POST`, `PATCH`, `DELETE`, `OPTIONS`.
- Headers: `Content-Type`, `Authorization`.
- `maxAge`: 86400.

`docs/DEPLOYMENT_NOTES.md` §4 explains why this is a function. Hono treats array entries as literal strings, so wildcard entries like `https://*.workers.dev` never match.

**Adding a custom domain**

Add one more condition to the `if (...)` at `worker/src/index.ts:23-27`. For example:

```ts
origin === 'https://play.example.com' ||
```

Use the exact scheme and host, with no trailing slash. Use `origin.endsWith('.example.com')` only if you want every subdomain allowed. A bare `endsWith('example.com')` would also match `evilexample.com`.

Then redeploy the Worker. I found no other origin allowlist in `worker/wrangler.toml` or the route files.

One thing to check: `SETUP.md:89` says the frontend needs no API-URL environment variable because it proxies same-origin. `docs/DEPLOYMENT_NOTES.md` §1 describes a build-time `NG_APP_API_URL` that points the browser at the Worker URL. If the browser calls the Worker directly from the new domain, the CORS change is needed. I didn't verify which setup the frontend actually uses.
